parameters.content:
# Local Video Production

Render narrated vertical videos on your computer, review the exact MP4, and publish approved drafts to Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts through n8n.

## How it works
- Create a brief in the local gallery; the worker renders and uploads a verified MP4.
- Watch the video, listen to its audio and approve the exact file and destinations.
- Scheduled slots publish eligible drafts and retain per-channel receipts for recovery.

## Customization
- Edit text, images, layout and narration language in the gallery.
- Choose channels and earliest publishing time.
- Match backend timezone/hours with the n8n schedules.

## Requirements
- V1 companion runtime: Python 3.10+, Node.js 22+, FFmpeg/ffprobe and persistent storage.
- SSH, Meta/YouTube OAuth, account IDs and signed HTTPS webhooks.
- A running worker; open its gallery at http://127.0.0.1:3850/ on that computer.

## Additional info

- [Version-specific README and package files](https://github.com/paoloronco/n8n-templates/blob/main/workflows/social/video-production/V1/README.md)
- [Detailed configuration and recovery](https://github.com/paoloronco/n8n-templates/blob/main/workflows/social/video-production/V1/documentation.md)
- Start with **YouTube only + private test**; Instagram tests publish publicly.
- Keep the workflow inactive and backend publishing disabled during setup.
- [Full documentation: setup, validation and recovery](https://paoloronco.notion.site/41cf0ba27c32816a8f5afafed8269368)

## 1. Render and review private drafts

This optional manual branch queues four sample briefs, waits for the PC worker and returns gallery links. Edit **Choose formats and audience** before running it.

Polling reuses each job ID; a new manual execution creates a new batch. Review existing jobs before repeating it. The gallery opens on the rendering computer.

## 2. Exchange signed worker jobs

The PC polls this HTTPS route to claim, renew or finish a job. n8n checks the envelope; the backend verifies its signature, expiry, nonce and lease before returning a receipt.

## 3. Check the approved queue

At **09:00 Europe/Rome**, report up to five approved, ready drafts. This branch creates and approves no videos.

Publishing slots run separately at **10, 12, 15, 18 and 21**. An empty or ineligible queue returns a no-op.

## 4. Claim a slot and deliver Instagram

Claim one due, approved video. The backend plans the next Meta action, saves its receipt and polls the same container until verified.

Unselected Instagram targets are skipped, including private YouTube tests. The final gate continues only when an approved YouTube target is prepared. Uncertain writes require reconciliation.

## 7. Receive the worker's verified MP4

Authorize the signed upload for its exact job and lease, restore the original binary and store it in the restricted upload directory. The backend checks its hash, decodes video/audio and acknowledges only a valid file. Uploading is separate from human approval.

## 8. Serve an authorized media URL

Instagram fetches the approved MP4 through this HTTPS route. The backend verifies the signed URL and expiry, then returns the allowed file path. n8n serves only those original bytes with no-store headers.

## 9. Resume only the incomplete channel

Persist the error and any existing YouTube ID. Use **Resume youtube** in the local gallery after fixing the cause.

An uncertain upload without an ID requires operator reconciliation. Keep successful channel receipts and verify an existing upload before retrying.

## Diagnose the backend

Run this standalone SSH node to inspect queue counts, worker heartbeat and free disk. It does not render or publish a video.

## 5. Upload the approved MP4 to YouTube

Check the OAuth channel against your configured ID and claim the approved original file. Upload once, save the returned video ID, then continue with that ID.

An existing ID resumes verification. Private tests use YouTube alone; the dry-run branch performs no upload.

## 6. Verify processing and save the result

Read the saved ID and check processing, channel, approved visibility, vertical dimensions and audio-stream metadata. Pending videos wait before another read; failures enter the recovery band below.

Save success only after verification. Platform metadata does not judge narration quality or guarantee Shorts classification.
